title: Question 1 (Intersectionwise χ-guarding)
statement_text: Which graph classes have the property that their graph-intersection with every $\chi$-bounded class of graphs is $\chi$-bounded?
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple, and classes are hereditary (closed under isomorphism and induced subgraphs). A class $\mathcal{C}$ is $\chi$-bounded if there is a non-decreasing $f$ with $\chi(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for all $G\in\mathcal{C}$. The intersection of graphs $G_1,\dots,G_k$ is $(\bigcap_iV(G_i),\bigcap_iE(G_i))$, and the graph-intersection $\mathcal{G}_1\cap\dots\cap\mathcal{G}_k$ of classes is the class of all graphs $G_1\cap\dots\cap G_k$ with $G_i\in\mathcal{G}_i$. A class $\mathcal{A}$ is intersectionwise $\chi$-guarding if $\mathcal{A}\cap\mathcal{B}$ is $\chi$-bounded for every $\chi$-bounded class $\mathcal{B}$. Graph-union preserves $\chi$-boundedness (Gyárfás), but graph-intersection does not: intersection graphs of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^k$ form the $k$-fold graph-intersection of the class of interval graphs (which are perfect), and this is $\chi$-bounded for $k=2$ (Asplund and Grünbaum) but not for $k=3$ (Burling). The authors prove that decomposable classes (every graph is a union of $t$ graphs, each admitting a $k$-colouring whose colour classes induce graphs whose components have independence number less than $r$, for fixed $t,k,r$) are intersectionwise $\chi$-guarding, e.g. unit interval graphs and line graphs of bipartite graphs; that some $\chi$-bounded classes, such as trivially perfect graphs, are not; they derive necessary conditions on a finite set $\mathcal{H}$ for $\mathcal{H}$-free graphs to be intersectionwise $\chi$-guarding, and show that $H$-free graphs are intersectionwise $\chi$-guarding if and only if $H$ is $P_2$, $P_3$ or $rK_1$. The authors also study the companion notion of intersectionwise self-$\chi$-guarding classes, whose $k$-fold graph-intersections are $\chi$-bounded for every $k$.
